name: Fight Colorectal Cancer
mission: We fight to cure colorectal cancer and serve as relentless champions of hope for all affected by this disease through informed patient support, impactful policy change, and breakthrough research endeavors.
theoryOfChange: Fight Colorectal Cancer has published "Path to a Cure 2026," which serves as a visionary roadmap and national blueprint for accelerating equitable, patient-centered progress against colorectal cancer (CRC). This document synthesizes the state of CRC research and care, highlights scientific momentum, exposes funding gaps, and charts a path forward. It outlines 2026-2028 priorities, such as funding diverse cohort studies, implementing universal Lynch syndrome testing, and supporting vaccine research. It also sets measurable targets, including achieving an 80% screening rate for average-risk patients and ensuring 80% of patients with abnormal non-invasive results receive a colonoscopy within 90 days.

rich_narrative.summary: Fight Colorectal Cancer (Fight CRC) is a national advocacy organization established in <cite id="3">2005</cite> that drives policy advocacy, research funding, and patient education [3]. In FY2025 filings, the organization reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $3,060,301</cite> while filing a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 81.4%</cite> [1, 2]. Based on its financial evaluations, its baseline program spending ratio was evaluated at <cite id="1">81%</cite> [1]. The charity holds a <cite id="1">98/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> and a Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid [1]. While Fight CRC demonstrates strong advocacy achievements, such as securing <cite id="4">$1,000,000 in research funding</cite> and supporting <cite id="4">1,700 clinics</cite>, it experiences financial deficits where expenses exceed total revenue, alongside executive compensation that represents a substantial portion of revenue [2, 4].
